regions.name: Amazon Rainforest
regions.line: The largest rainforest on Earth, threaded by the world's greatest river system.

regions.name: Pantanal
regions.line: A seasonal flood plain where wildlife gathers at the water's edge.

regions.name: Central American Forests
regions.line: Cloud forest and lowland jungle on the land bridge between two continents.

regions.name: Andes & Patagonia
regions.line: The longest mountain chain on land, falling away to windswept southern steppe.

regions.name: Galápagos Islands
regions.line: Young volcanic islands whose isolated animals helped inspire the theory of evolution.

regions.name: North American Deserts
regions.line: The Sonoran, Mojave and Chihuahuan: heat, cactus and animals that wait for rain.

regions.name: North American Forests & Rockies
regions.line: Mountain forest and open prairie, home of the bison and the wolf.

regions.name: Arctic Tundra
regions.line: Treeless, frozen ground that blooms for a few short weeks each summer.

regions.name: Sahara & Arabian Deserts
regions.line: The largest hot desert in the world, and its sand seas across the Red Sea.

regions.name: African Savanna
regions.line: Grassland of East and Southern Africa, home to the greatest herds left on Earth.

regions.name: Congo Basin & Albertine Rift
regions.line: Africa's great rainforest, and the volcanic mountains of the Rift at its edge.

regions.name: Namib & Kalahari
regions.line: A coastal desert watered by fog, beside a vast red semi-desert.

regions.name: Madagascar
regions.line: An island cut off for 88 million years, where most animals live nowhere else.

regions.name: Indian Subcontinent
regions.line: Monsoon forest and tall grassland shaped by the rains.

regions.name: Himalaya & Tibetan Plateau
regions.line: The roof of the world, where animals live in thin air and deep cold.

regions.name: China, Gobi & Mongolian Steppe
regions.line: Bamboo mountain forest giving way to steppe and cold desert.

regions.name: Siberian Taiga & Russian Far East
regions.line: The largest forest on Earth: conifers, snow and long winters.

regions.name: European Forests & Mountains
regions.line: Old woodland and alpine peaks where lost animals are returning.

regions.name: Borneo & Sumatra
regions.line: Ancient island rainforest, among the richest and most threatened on Earth.

regions.name: Australian Outback
regions.line: Red, dry interior of a continent that has evolved its own animals.

regions.name: Eastern Australia, Tasmania & New Guinea
regions.line: Eucalypt forest, tropical rainforest and the egg-laying mammals.

regions.name: Antarctica
regions.line: The coldest continent, where life clings to the edge of the sea ice.

regions.name: Pacific Ocean
regions.line: The largest and deepest ocean, home to its deepest trenches.

regions.name: Atlantic Ocean
regions.line: A young, widening ocean stretching from pole to pole.

regions.name: Indian Ocean
regions.line: Warm, monsoon-driven water and some of the richest reefs on Earth.

regions.name: Southern Ocean
regions.line: Cold, stormy water circling Antarctica, rich in krill.

regions.name: Arctic Ocean
regions.line: A small, ice-covered ocean at the top of the world.
